doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Carolina campus bands and leaving college for music
summary: Transferring to North Carolina, playing in the Tarheels with Bix Ramsey, and dropping out; Biagini and the Casa Loma background.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What band was that? Was that one of the early groups?

That was a band that originated at the University of North Carolina. That’s where I went after my freshman year in college of Davison. I transferred there — because they had a much bigger school there, they also had a music school, which I didn’t go. But they had campus bands, like that’s where Hal Kemp first started. And it’s also where Kay Kyser came from. And more opportunity to play. By this time I really wanted to play, and on the campus, when I transferred there as a sophomore, there was a trumpet — the band was The Carolina Tarheels they called them. And they had a trumpet player, Bix Ramsey. So I asked him, I said, “Why do they call you Bix?” He said, “Because I play so much like Bix.” He was kind of a — I won’t say dumb — but he was a good player, and funny. He wrote out some stuff that Bix played, note for note, and I finally played in that band with him, and we dropped out of school several times. And that’s how it just kept going like that.
Did you kind of give up college to go out and pursue your music?

I gave up college for three years when I was in bands, and then I went back to college for another, well I guess a full year. And by that time, well I never did go back to get a degree, because I had music jobs that I wanted to keep playing, ones from unknown bands, to, I wound up, some fellow had a band in 1936. Normally you would know about Hank Biagini — well Hank Biagini was from Detroit and he had the original Casa Loma band, which was actually Jean Goldkette — that name?
